content.title: About
content.content: Fresh potato hash brown are made from boiled potatoes that are shredded, formed into small patties and fried until golden and crisp. They have a mild potato flavor, a crunchy outer crust and a soft interior. Hash browns are commonly served as a side dish for breakfast, lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally hash brown are made from raw grated potato, but the fresh version uses cooked potato for a softer interior.
In the United States hash brown are a staple in fast‑food restaurants and school cafeterias.
They can be flavored with onion, herbs or cheese to vary the taste.
Hash brown are believed to have originated in the early 20th century as a way to use leftover boiled potatoes.
In some countries they are served with sour cream or yogurt dip.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Potatoes provide complex carbohydrates that supply sustained energy.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Fresh potatoes contain vitamin C, which supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Hash browns retain dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low fat when prepared properly
items.content: If cooked with minimal oil or baked, they can be a moderately low‑calorie option.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When fried, salt is often added; excessive sodium intake can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: High‑temperature frying can produce acrylamide, a potential toxin; moderate heat or baking is recommended.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid blood sugar spikes in diabetics.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hash browns can be enjoyed as a snack, served alongside eggs, omelets, salads, or used in burgers. They reheat well in the oven or skillet to restore crispness. Garnish with fresh herbs and serve with sour cream or yogurt dip if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked hash browns in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a separate bag; reheating in the oven will keep the crust crispy.
